newsitem.title: KENYA: NAIROBI SHARES CLOSE LOWER, BOND MARKET PICKS UP.
newsitem.headline: NAIROBI SHARES CLOSE LOWER, BOND MARKET PICKS UP.

text.p: The Nairobi bourse share index dropped on Monday but there was renewed trading in bonds, bourse officials said.

The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-Share index fell 17.3 points to close at 3406.57 from 3423.87. Turnover was stable with 11.4 million shillings traded on 296,000 shares from 11.3 million shillings dealt on 237,021 shares.
"There were no special deals, most of the activity was on the normal boards," a stock exchange official told Reuters.

Senior brokers said Monday's renewed activity in the secondary bond market was due to local investors buying ahead of an anticipated increase in the yield offered on treasury bills- to which the floating-rate bond is pegged.
Some 1,680,000 shillings of the fourth issue of the Central Bank of Kenya floating-rate treasury bond were traded at 102.4274 percent from 102.2968 percent.
While 100,300,000 of the third issue of the bond was traded at 102.5506 percent from 102.550 percent.

On the agricultural board 7,000 Sasini Tea and Coffee changed hands at 81.50 shillings from 80.00. Rea Vipingo Plantations sold 8,700 shares at between 8.5 shillings and 8.8 from 80 at Friday's close.

The commercial and services sector saw the biggest slice of Monday's action, accounting for 41 percent of Monday's volume. Uchumi Supermarkets was busy at between 38 and 39 shillings, for 43,600 shares.
Nation Printers and Publishers continued to gain, adding three shillings to close at 120, selling 1,752 shares.
Trading was brisk on the finance and investment board, with Barclays Bank moving up a shilling to close at 107. Kenya Commercial Bank closed unchanged at 98.
It was a good day for Kenya Breweries which edged up to 55 from 54, traded on 626 shares. But Total Kenya took a beating, losing four shillings to close on 64.
